explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a cross‑platform desktop application named “res‑downloader,” built with Go (backend) and Vue (frontend) via the Wails framework.  
   - Purpose: provide a GUI tool that runs a local proxy, intercepts/sniffs various media resources (video, audio, images, live streams), and downloads them.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top‑level:  
     • core/ – Go packages implementing app logic, HTTP proxy, downloader, resource parsing, storage, cross‑platform system hooks, logging, middleware.  
     • frontend/ – Vue3/Vite/TypeScript UI, components, stores, router, assets, Wails JS runtime glue.  
     • build/ – Platform‑specific build outputs and installer scripts for macOS, Linux (AppImage, Arch, Debian), Windows (NSIS).  
     • main.go, wails.json – entrypoint and Wails config.  
     • docs/ – static site for user docs, examples, troubleshooting.  

3. Insights from README  
   - The app spins up a system proxy (127.0.0.1:8899), filters HTTP(s) traffic for supported platforms, parses out resource URLs, displays them.  
   - UI triggers backend APIs to start/stop proxy, select resource types, decrypt or download.  
   - Packages for all desktop OSes are generated via Wails and native installers.

4. Creating the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
      1. Frontend (Vue3 UI)  
      2. Wails runtime bridge (JS ↔ Go)  
      3. Go backend  
         – Proxy server module  
         – Resource sniffer/parser module  
         – Download manager module  
         – Storage module (local file system or embedded DB)  
         – Config & logging  
         – OS abstraction layer (core/system_*.go)  
      4. External network (websites, streaming hosts)  
      5. Local file system (download location, config, logs)  
      6. Platform package installers (build outputs)  
   b. Relationships & interactions  
      - UI → (Wails RPC) → Backend APIs (e.g., StartProxy, FetchResources, Download)  
      - Backend Proxy listens on 127.0.0.1:8899 ← User’s browser/OS network stack  
      - Proxy forwards allowed traffic to External Network, inspects responses, extracts resource metadata  
      - Sniffer module publishes resource events → Frontend via Wails event bus  
      - Download manager fetches resource URLs → writes to Local FS via Storage module  
      - OS abstraction handles certificate installation, proxy config, file dialogs  
   c. Architectural patterns/design principles  
      - Layered separation: UI layer, API/bridge layer, core service layer, platform‑specific layer  
      - Observer/event‑driven for resource discovery (backend emits events → UI updates store → re‑renders)  
      - Modular Go packages grouped by concern (proxy, downloader, storage, system)  
      - MVVM-style in Vue: components bind to reactive stores (Pinia)  
   d. Key technologies & libraries  
      - Go modules: wailsapp/wails, net/http (proxy), custom downloader logic  
      - Vue3 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS  
      - Pinia for state management, Vue Router  
      - Wails JS runtime for RPC and bundling  
      - NSIS, AppImage tooling, native packaging for cross‑platform distribution

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full‑stack desktop app  
   - Clearly show the separation between the Vue-based frontend and the Go backend, connected by the Wails runtime.  
   - Emphasize the internal proxy loop: UI control → backend starts proxy → system network uses proxy → backend inspects traffic → UI displays resources.  
   - Highlight the file I/O path: download request → backend downloader → storage module → local disk.  
   - Indicate packaging flow: source → Wails build → native installer per OS.

6. Diagram notation guidelines  
   - Label each box: e.g., “Vue3 UI,” “Wails RPC Bridge,” “Proxy Server,” “Downloader,” “Storage,” “OS Abstraction,” “External Network,” “Local FS.”  
   - Use arrows with direction and brief label: e.g., “RPC call,” “HTTP proxy,” “Resource events,” “File write.”  
   - Color‑code layers:  
     • UI layer (blue)  
     • Bridge/API layer (orange)  
     • Core backend (green)  
     • External systems (gray)  
   - Use distinct shapes: rectangles for components, cylinders for storage, cloud icons for external network.

7. Key points to capture in detail  
   - The dual role of the backend as both an HTTP proxy and a download engine.  
   - Wails as the glue between Go services and the JS UI.  
   - OS‑specific hooks for certificate and proxy configuration.  
   - Build and packaging artifacts per platform.

By following these guidelines, the diagram will clearly convey the end‑to‑end architecture: from user interactions in the Vue UI, through Wails RPC into Go services, through the proxy sniffing loop, to resource downloads and storage—all within a packaged desktop application.  
</explanation>
